appraisal_events.evidence: Swann, avec son ostentation, avec sa manière de crier sur les toits ses moindres relations, était un vulgaire esbroufeur que le Marquis de Norpois eût sans doute trouvé...«puant»; the narrator goes on to detail how Swann now loudly advertises trivial new connections gained through Odette after formerly concealing his most brilliant ones.
appraisal_events.explanation: The father's harsh verdict that Swann has become a vulgar show-off is substantiated at length by the narrator, who traces the change to Swann's marriage and his construction of a new, lesser social position built around Odette's circle.

appraisal_events.evidence: Les plus intelligents des jeunes médecins déclarèrent...que si jamais ils tombaient malades, Cottard était le seul maître auquel ils confieraient leur peau; devenu, à la longue, notoriété européenne.
appraisal_events.explanation: Contrary to his earlier reputation for mediocrity, Cottard is shown to command genuine esteem among his most discerning colleagues for his diagnostic skill, reversing the family's outdated impression of him.

status_effects.explanation: Swann is portrayed, with narrator corroboration, as having become vain and ostentatious about trivial new connections, a clear decline from his formerly discreet elegance.
His new social position, built to suit Odette's more modest circle, is explicitly described as beneath the brilliant one he held before his marriage.
Cottard's professional standing is clearly elevated as his most discerning colleagues recognize him as an outstanding diagnostician, correcting an earlier impression of mediocrity.

ambiguities: The narrator's elaboration on Swann's new vanity partly softens the father's blunt condemnation by comparing him to modest, well-regarded artists who become naively proud of a late-life hobby; it is not fully certain whether this qualifies as full narratorial endorsement of the father's harshness or a more sympathetic recontextualization of it.
